Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited. GSMA Mobile Connectivity Index 2025 (reported by Ecofin Agency, January 2026) puts Libya's 4G population coverage at 83.7%, up from 76.8% in early 2023 (GSMA/Speedtest Intelligence via GSMA member blog and ts2.tech) and 40% per ITU's 2021 estimate. The most recent, most authoritative figure (83.7%) falls in the 75–89% band, i.e. code 4, not 90%+ (code 5), so the value code is revised downward.

Definition: Affordability of electricity for residential and small business consumers, measured as cost of electricity relative to income levels. High electricity costs are a direct barrier to ICT adoption and data center viability.
Comments: Electricity is free or very low cost 0.007 USD/kWh
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited but the claim is confirmed independently: residential electricity tariffs are approximately US$0.007–0.008/kWh, described by the IMF (Selected Issues Paper, July 2025) and Libya Tribune/Minbar Libya (July 2025) as among the lowest in the world and heavily subsidised (total energy subsidy bill ~US$17bn in 2024). At this tariff, even high household consumption represents well under 1% of GNI per capita, supporting 'Very Affordable (<1%)'. Value code 5 confirmed unchanged.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
Comments: Off-grid solar limited due to oil dependency
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited, and the claim of 'no policy framework' is contradicted by evidence found. Libya's Renewable Energy Authority (REAOL) launched the National Strategy for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency (2023–2035) with USAID support in December 2023, alongside the 'Go Green' initiative — residential, public-facility, agricultural and industrial rooftop-solar programmes targeting 500MW of distributed PV — confirmed on REAOL's own website and in USAID Libya newsletters (August 2024). Independent legal analyses (Chambers, Mondaq, Tumi Law Firm) note the broader renewable framework remains fragmented with no feed-in tariff, so this is an active but still nascent policy rather than a comprehensive one. Revised to code 3 (Active policy with some deployment).
